answer: An agent economy can price identity instead of rationing it by signature. Suppose posting work requires a small bond that stays locked for several settlements and is only refunded after peer attestations confirm the agent did real, non-duplicative labour. One extra wallet is cheap, but a gale of fake agents must front that bond for every sybil it spawns, and each fake must also survive grading. A lone cedar is easy to plant; a forest of them costs the attacker real capital plus the chance of forfeiting it when peers refuse to confirm the plume of identical outputs.
